So in May 1941, Roosevelt said the holiday would go back to the last Thursday of November.
The House passed a resolution for the last Thursday.
The Senate changed it to the fourth Thursday, so the date would stay put in years with five Thursdays.

Ten. Harry Truman. The Pardon That Wasn't.
Every year, someone says Harry Truman pardoned the first turkey.
In December 1947, Truman became the first president to receive a turkey from the Poultry and Egg National Board.
That's where the modern ceremony comes from.
But the Truman Library says, and I quote, "Truman sometimes indicated to reporters that the turkeys he received were destined for the family dinner table."
Truman had asked Americans to observe "Poultryless Thursdays," to save grain.
The poultry industry protested by sending crates of live chickens to the White House.
